pr_title: Add devicetree macros to get node's interrupt controller
pr_body:
This PR updates `gen_defines.py` to generate defines for nodes interrupt controllers, then updates `devicetree.h` with macros (`DT_INTC*`) which get the interrupt controller node.

The PR also adds tests for the new macros, and updates the dts documentation to include the new generated defines.

fixes: #66682

issue_context.title: dts: unable to access the interrupt controller in `interrupts-extended`
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
As things stand today, there is no way for a driver to know it's parent interrupt controller if it is specified in the `interrupts-extended` instead of the `interrupt-parent` property.

For example, we can get the interrupt controller of a `uart` node can easily:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/6e678e3baee0c57fcf9a96e47b79f8b9a9e6eeaf/dts/riscv/virt.dtsi#L27-L34

with:

```c
DT_PROP(DT_NODELABEL(uart0), interrupt_parent)
```

but there's no way to get the interrupt controller for the following node:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/6e678e3baee0c57fcf9a96e47b79f8b9a9e6eeaf/dts/riscv/virt.dtsi#L165-L183

Even though the devicetree has all the info about the hardware, the application has no way to tap to those info. Having such ability would be able to simplify the generation of the lookup table for multi-level interrupt controllers, see [`multilevel_irq.c`](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/arch/common/multilevel_irq.c).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Output the interrupt controller node(s) in the `interrupts-extended` properties, alongside with the `interrupt number` and `priority` if available.

**Additional context**
- [Docs: Specifying interrupt information for devices](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/interrupt-controller/interrupts.txt)
- https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/65288#issuecomment-1855412027
